entry.description: Matches an option on gist when two options differ by a single word.
entry.childHint: Two answers can look almost the same. Find what differs and check it against the text.
entry.approvalNote: Cleared on the printed review pack; returned marked up.

textProvenance.note: Ruled when written; absent from the store until now (R403/R410).
textProvenance.authority: annie-seventyseventh-return.md, read from the file, sha256 1c7070f52f67c5d9664f26f1fdefa17323ff1b9111a84ca7c4d093c8c48f79a7

stem.text: Read line 49: 'A grave round face'. What does 'grave' mean here?

options.value: Serious and calm.
A place where someone is buried.
Dark and dirty with earth.
Very sad and upset.
Round and rather fat.
options.execution: 'Grave' is skimmed as a near-neighbour of 'round', which is the very next word on the line.

stem.text: Read lines 66 to 67. What does the last thing the Mole says show about his day?

carriers.key: The whole day had been full of things he had never done before.

options.value: He was hoping the Rat would let him hold the oars.
He was still frightened of the water.
The whole day had been full of things he had never done before.
He was already wishing he was back in his own house.
He had been in boats before, but never one as fine as this.
options.execution: Line 67 reads 'never been in a boat before in all my life'. This keeps the sentence's shape and its 'never', moves the never onto the boat's fineness, and so reverses what line 67 says about him.

stem.text: Read lines 17 to 23. Who actually came into the assembly-room with Mr Bingley?

carriers.key: His two sisters, the husband of the elder sister, and one other young man.

options.value: His five sisters and a cousin.
Twelve ladies and seven gentlemen.
His two sisters, Mr Hurst and Mr Bennet.
options.execution: One name changed: Mr Bennet for the young man. Everything else matches line 22.

options.value: His two sisters and both their husbands.
His two sisters, the husband of the elder sister, and one other young man.

stem.text: Read lines 24 to 34. Line 24 uses 'countenance' about Mr Bingley and line 34 about Mr Darcy. What does it mean both times?

carriers.key: A person's face, and the look on it.

options.value: A person's face, and the look on it.
The way a person speaks to other people.
Letting something happen, or agreeing to it.
The good name a person's family has in the county.
A count of how many people are in a room.
options.execution: 'Countenance' is skimmed for the word 'count' inside it.

stem.text: Read lines 39 to 41. How many dances did Mr Darcy dance, and who did he dance with?

carriers.key: Two: one with Mrs Hurst and one with Miss Bingley.

options.value: Every dance of the evening.
Two: one with Mrs Hurst and one with Miss Bingley.
Two: one with Miss Bingley and one with Elizabeth.
options.execution: One name changed: Elizabeth for Mrs Hurst. The count and the shape of line 40 are kept.

options.value: None at all.
Three: with Mrs Hurst, Miss Bingley and Miss Bennet.

stem.text: Read lines 57 to 59. Mr Bingley cries: 'I would not be so fastidious as you are.' What does 'fastidious' mean here?

options.value: Very hard to please.
Very quick and in a hurry.
options.execution: 'Fastidious' is skimmed as though it were 'fast'.

options.value: Very shy with people you do not know.
Very tidy and neat.
Very rude to other people.

stem.text: What did Matthew do when he first saw the girl? (lines 4 to 6)

carriers.key: He slipped past her without looking at her.

options.value: He slipped past her without looking at her.
He noticed her red hair and freckled face.
He asked her who she was waiting for.
He slipped past her, glancing at her as he went.
options.execution: Differs from the key by one element: line 5 says without looking at her.

stem.text: What does the girl do once she decides Matthew is coming to her? (lines 47 to 49)

carriers.key: She stands up, takes her bag and holds out her hand.

options.value: She stands up, takes her bag and holds out her hand.
She stays sitting and watches him come closer.
She stands up and holds out both her hands.
options.execution: Differs by one detail: line 48 puts the bag in one hand and only the other is held out.

options.value: She walks along the platform to meet him.

stem.text: What does Matthew ask the girl to do at the end? (lines 64 and 65)

carriers.key: Come along with him, and hand him her bag.

options.value: Go and sit in the ladies' waiting room.
Come along with him, and carry her own bag.
options.execution: Differs by one detail: line 65 asks her to give him the bag.

options.value: Tell him her name before they set off.
Come along with him, and hand him her bag.

stem.text: Why did Beauty like going in the dog-cart? (lines 2 and 3)

carriers.key: It was light, and its high wheels ran along pleasantly.

options.value: It was light, and its high wheels ran along pleasantly.
It was the only cart he was strong enough to pull.
It meant John came with him instead of the master.
It was slow, so the journey felt easy.
options.execution: Differs by one word: line 3 says light, not slow.

stem.text: What came down across the road in front of them? (lines 22 to 24)

carriers.key: An oak tree, torn up by the roots.

options.value: An oak tree, torn up by the roots.
A great branch from one of the swaying trees.
options.execution: Line 20 names a branch as John's worry; line 23 says a whole oak came down.

options.value: Part of the wooden bridge, carried off by the flood.
A shower of dry leaves blown across the road.

stem.text: What does Uncle Podger send Jim to Mr Goggles for? (lines 13 and 14)

options.value: To borrow his step-ladder.
options.execution: The step-ladder is in the same speech at line 12, but Uncle Podger wants that himself.

options.value: To tell him that Pa's leg is better.
To borrow his spirit-level.
To fetch a bit of picture-cord.

stem.text: What does Uncle Podger fall onto when the string slips? (lines 43 to 45)

options.value: The piano.
The kitchen-chair he had been standing on.
options.execution: The chair is real at line 42, but line 44 says he slides down onto the piano.

options.value: The charwoman's corns.
Somebody's toes, with a yell.

stem.text: What was the bin bag for? (lines 7 to 9)

carriers.key: Anything with the sole coming off it.

options.value: Anything with the sole coming off it.
Anything with no name in it.
options.execution: Line 8 gives unnamed things to the second box, not the bag.

options.value: Anything going to the charity collection.
Anything that smelled of chlorine.

stem.text: Read lines 4 and 5. What do they say about Saltmere and this walk?

carriers.key: He got as far as the caravan park, twice.

options.value: He got as far as Saltmere, twice.
options.execution: One word out: line 5 says the caravan park, which is where the bus stops.

options.value: He got as far as the caravan park, twice.
He had never set out for Saltmere before.
He walked out to Saltmere about four years ago.

stem.text: Look at lines 1 and 2. Where does Jane sit down?

carriers.key: On a stile that leads into a field.

options.value: On a stile that leads into a field.
In the field on the other side of the stile.
On a low wall beside the frozen causeway.
On a stile that leads into a lane.
options.execution: One word out: line 2 says the stile led into a field.
